findings.note: The bill page lists Barnes among the sponsors of SB 356, titled Constitutional Amendment/Photo ID. Edition 3 (House committee substitute, 6/26/24, text at https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2023/Bills/Senate/HTML/S356v3.html) would amend the State Constitution so that voters must present photographic identification before voting, in the text's words 'NOT JUST THOSE PRESENTING TO VOTE IN PERSON'. The filed edition was a different subject (motor vehicle dealers), so the page's sponsor list is shown as it appears; the date is the last edition date, not the date she signed on. Last action: sent back to House rules committee 6/27/2024.

SB 88, Various Elections Changes, lists Barnes among its sponsors. Edition 3 (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2023/Bills/Senate/HTML/S88v3.html) would require county boards to challenge ballots of ineligible voters due to death or felony conviction, and require signature verification for executed absentee ballots, including a signature-matching pilot program.

findings.motion: SB 88 Various Elections Changes, Third Reading, roll call S-620, passed 28-19
findings.note: Roll-call transcript lists Barnes among the Ayes on third reading of SB 88 (signature verification for absentee ballots, challenges to ineligible voters due to death or felony conviction).

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading, roll call S-693, passed 28-13
findings.note: Roll-call transcript lists Barnes among the Ayes. Edition 8 of HB 958 (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/HTML/H958v8.html) includes a section on the State Board of Elections acting on 'potential non-eligible citizens appearing on the State's voter registration records from a federal database', plus changes to voter list maintenance and drivers-license-office voter registration. Her vote record also shows Aye on Amendment 1 (S-684) and on tabling motions for Amendments 2, 3 and 6 to 10 the same day.

Senate second-reading vote on HB 958, Election Law Changes (roll call 2026-07-28, 6:13 PM): Barnes voted Aye, 28 to 13. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) adds G.S. 163-83, under which a county board processes a registration application only if it affirmatively says the applicant is a U.S. citizen. A blank answer gets a notice, and a statement under penalty of perjury is required within 30 days. It also bars driver-license-office staff from proceeding with a registration unless the applicant says they are a citizen, and it requires a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens in a federal database. The bill page shows the bill was vetoed 2026-08-17. She also voted Aye on Amendment 1 and Aye on Amendment 5, and Aye on motions to table Amendments 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
